title: tenant-fallback-cost-orchestrator-and-weighted-prefill-policy
author: Anya Patel
description: Motivation: customer tenants with spiky traffic were experiencing larger-than-expected unit cost due to conservative batching and lack of tenant-aware fallback routing. This PR implements a Tenant Fallback Cost Orchestrator: a runtime policy layer that (1) computes a lightweight tenant-level cost signal from recent per-token latency and batch-utilization telemetry, (2) applies tenant weighting to prefer cheaper compatible model variants and relaxed batching thresholds under budget constraints, and (3) integrates a safe fallback policy to preserve latency SLOs. High-level changes: added orchestrator shim that sits between request router and model selector; tenant cost signal aggregator using existing metrics streams; new policy DSL for weighted prefill and fallback rules; integration tests and end-to-end smoke tests; a small CLI to simulate tenant budget thresholds locally. Checklist: - [x] Core orchestrator implementation - [x] Telemetry aggregator and signal smoothing - [x] Policy DSL and default tenant-weighted rules - [x] Unit and integration tests - [x] Backwards compatible default (no change unless tenant opts in) - [x] Documentation: console runbook and API example Compatibility and safety: defaults are opt-in per-tenant; fallbacks maintain a strict latency cap and will never route to lower-quality quantized variants unless tenant-level override is enabled; the orchestrator exposes a dry-run mode for operators. Rollout plan: gated canary on 10 internal tenants, monitor unit cost and P95 latency for 48 hours, expand to 50% of production tenants, then full deploy. Related work: builds on sampling primitives from ENG-3120 and policy DSL from ENG-2974.
